newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Duma passes seven mineral deposits for PSAs.
newsitem.headline: Russia Duma passes seven mineral deposits for PSAs.

text.p: Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament passed a bill on Friday in its first reading which lists seven mineral reserves exploitable under production sharing agreements.
The bill must go through three readings to pass into law.

The seven deposits were the Samotlor oil and gas condensate deposit, the Krasnoleninskoye oil deposit, the Kuranakh group of gold deposits, the Yakovlevskoye iron ore deposit, the Romanshkinskoye oil deposit, deposits in the northern sector of Sakhalin island and the Prirazlomnoye oil deposit on the shelf of the Barents Sea.
The State Duma voted down a list containing these seven deposits on April 25.
Only two of the deposits on the list of seven will be open to development with foreign companies -- the Kuranakh gold reserves and the Prirazlomnoye oil deposit.

But investment in the fields over the life of proposed projects is expected to reach $16 billion, and could boost Russian oil output by an average of 30 million tonnes (600,000 barrels per day) eventually.
This is 10 percent of Russia's total output.
Some key oil fields targeted by foreign oil companies for development have yet to be debated by the Duma.
